newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa to issue $85 mln in convertible notes.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa to issue $85 mln in convertible notes.

text.p: Mexico's biggest steel firm Altos Hornos de Mexico SA de CV (Ahmsa) said on Tuesday it planned to issue $85 million in senior discount convertible notes maturing in 2001.

Ahmsa "announced today that it has filed a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with its contemplated offering of Senior Discount Convertible Notes due 2001, with a principal amount at maturity of $85 million," the company said in a statement.
Ahmsa said the notes would be offered primarily in the United States and would be convertible into American Depositary Shares with each ADS representing five shares of the firm's common stock.

"Application has been made for the listing of the notes and the ADSs on the New York Stock Exchange," Ahmsa said. "The offering price, interest rate, conversion price and other terms of the notes will be determined shortly before the offering."
Ahmsa said it would use the proceeds of the issue to pay short-term debt. Last week the company said that the issue would be carried out in the first half of 1997 at the latest.
The lead manager would be Merrill Lynch and Inverlat International Inc would be the co-manager, Ahmsa said.
